edbDesc: In optics, dispersion is the phenomenon in which the phase velocity of a wave depends on its frequency. Media having such a property are termed dispersive media. Dispersion is most often described for light waves, but it may occur for any kind of wave that interacts with a medium or passes through an inhomogeneous geometry (e.g. a waveguide), such as sound waves.
title: Dispersion (of waves)
pickWhy: Splitting white light into colours because each colour travels at a different speed is Newton's Prisms card.
